why: The pilot's cart, reviewed 2026-09-11 against v1.0.0 on the instrument that now reads Gishath's reveal. Seven adds for the audit's ramp surplus (15 vs 10-12) and its weakest interaction: Bloom Tender, Hunting Velociraptor, Savage Order, Up the Beanstalk, Savage Stomp, Molten Echoes, Chandra's Ignition. The goldfish sees Bloom Tender and Beanstalk's entry draw and nothing of prowl, the tutor-to-battlefield, the copies or the one-sided wipe, so its objective is a CONTROL on the clock (0.617 today): the four ramp cuts may not cost more than about two points. Forge at standard-v3 reads all seven and is the gate.

staged.why: a two-colour rock for a dork that makes all three; measured +3.1 turn-8 damage alone on the cart sweep
three-mana land ramp for a three-mana Dinosaur that makes every Dinosaur spell cost {2}{R} after a Dinosaur connects; Gishath has haste and the list has 21 Dinosaurs
a three-mana ramp body for a four-mana Dinosaur tutor straight onto the battlefield with indestructible; the sacrifice is a body the reveal gave for free
a pinging two-colour rock for a two-mana draw engine that triggers on every five-plus-mana spell; card advantage is 5 against a target of 10
three-mana removal on a body for one-mana fight with a counter on a Dinosaur
three-mana removal that gifts a 3/3 for a copy of every nontoken Dinosaur entering, including the four a game the reveal puts onto the battlefield
a six-mana symmetrical sweeper for a five-mana one-sided one: a 7-power Gishath deals seven to every other creature and each opponent

one turn of +7/+7 trample for a saga that does three: a free red or green creature the turn it lands, three counters on Gishath (a ten-card reveal), then double power (a twenty-card reveal); Gishath already tramples
